questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people who keep secrets are often unhappy and stressed
How some secrets can have a positive effect on us
The secret recipe of a famous soft drink
How to find out if someone is lying
questions.why: Neil says they'll be discussing the advantages of keeping secrets.

questions.q: What does Neil admit about keeping secrets?
options: He can never keep any secrets
He tells his friends everything
He's good at it, except with the endings of films
He doesn't like it when people tell him their secrets
questions.why: He's pretty good at it, “unless it's giving away the ending of a movie”.

questions.q: What do new psychological studies suggest about keeping good news to yourself?
options: It can energise you, especially if you'll share it later
It usually damages your relationships with family and friends
It makes people feel guilty and ashamed
It only works for very small secrets
questions.why: Neil says it can make you feel more alive, especially if you plan to share it later.

questions.q: Which is an example of a secret whose purpose is to be revealed?
options: A guilty pleasure
A lie that hurts another person
A family problem
A surprise marriage proposal
questions.why: Dr Slepian lists the surprising marriage proposal and the pregnancy announcement.

questions.q: Why do positive secrets give us energy, according to the research?
options: They make other people like and trust us more
They help us sleep better
They stop us feeling hungry
They make us feel in control of our emotions
questions.why: Neil says positive secrets give us the feeling we are in control of our emotions.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention that Dr Slepian's research comes from the United States?
options: To show that it is the most reliable study
To question whether the results apply to other cultures
To explain why Coca-Cola is so popular
To say that Americans keep more secrets than other people do
questions.why: He asks, “Would the results be the same in other cultures and countries?”

questions.q: What does Devina Gupta say happens in some cultures?
options: People wait to share pregnancy news in case it brings bad luck
People in most cultures announce a pregnancy as early as possible
Pregnancy is never discussed at all
Only grandparents are told about a pregnancy
questions.why: She says people don't share it until it's safe, fearing negative vibes or the evil eye.

questions.q: What does Dr Slepian think about pregnancy secrets?
options: They are always negative secrets
They are exactly the same in every culture around the world
Early on they feel like a burden, later more positive
They should be shared immediately
questions.why: He says earlier it looks more like a burdensome secret, later more like a positive one.
